To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the PDF4LHCr ecommendations are a reasonable choice for the LHC at 7 TeV and that, at this stage, the differences between the PDFs from different groups are small enough to be neglected in the context of the LHC at this energy, but the situation may well change in the future.

(a) the PDF4LHC group has recommended a common set of PDFs, which is based on the CTEQ, MRST and NNPDF collaborations, and (b) the PDF4LOHCrecommendations have a significant impact on the total W and Z production cross section at the LHC, and (c) the PDF4PDFs are not in agreement with each other for W and Z production at the LHC.

(1) the predictions for the W cross section are very stable with respect to PDF and scale variations; (2) the predictions for Z cross section are also stable with respect to the PDF variations, but show larger scale variations than the W predictions; (3) the predictions for Higgs production cross section are also very stable with respect both to the PDF and scale variations, and (4) the predictions for $ t\bar t$ cross section show large scale and PDF uncertainties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dependence of the Standard Model predictions on the choice of PDFs.

the dependence of the benchmark Standard Model cross sections at the Tevatron and LHC on the choice of the strong coupling constant αS(MZ), the PDFs, the PDF error sets and the PDF uncertainty treatment.
the following questions: How much do the different PDF sets differ from each other?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PDF4LHCRECOMMENDATIONS are a very good compromise, but that there remains room for further progress in the future.
the current level of agreement between theory and data is excellent, and the differences in predictions are smaller than the current experimental errors.
, at the present stage, the theoretical uncertainties in the total cross sections are larger than the experimental uncertainties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, for the W cross section at the LHC, the current data and theory agree within the experimental and theoretical uncertainties, and that the PDF4LHC recommendations are in agreement with the data and with each other.
the theoretical predictions are consistent with the current LHC measurements, and that there is still room for the LHC experiments to constrain the PDFs.
the current PDFs give predictions for W and Z production at the LHC which agree within 1.4% for W and 0.7% for Z, and that these predictions depend on the value of αS(MZ).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the theoretical uncertainties on the W and Z total cross sections, at the 7 TeV LHC, are significantly smaller than those on the top quark cross section.

the theoretical uncertainties due to the choice of PDFs are comparable to those due to the choice and value of αS(MZ), and are larger than those associated with the renormalisation and factorisation scales.
the PDF4LHC recommendation of the average of the CT10, MSTW08 and NNPDF2.3 PDF sets should be used for the W and Z cross-section predictions.
